description: Interpret the forcing process as a monotone cellular automaton on the product grid behind a constructible graph. Each cell stores a quotient module of reachable label vectors after modding out support already absorbed into T, and infection occurs when the anti-diagonal line intersects that local module.
mathematical_formalization: Let L_t <= (Z^2)^V be the submodule generated by the initial seeds R and all edge-difference generators exposed by G up to time t. Define T_{t+1} = T_t union {e in V : exists f in L_t with supp(f) subseteq T_t union {e} and f(e) = a(1,-1), a != 0}; the CA surrogate tracks M_t(e) = pi_e(L_t / (Z^2)^{T_t}).
analogical_connections: Bootstrap percolation where infection is algebraic rather than purely Boolean.
Gaussian elimination executed by local update rules on a lattice.
Reaction-diffusion with the anti-diagonal line acting as the trigger threshold.
implementation_hypothesis: Represent each local module by a small Smith-normal-form state or a reduced basis over bounded coefficients. Simulate updates on candidate d_1 x ... x d_k grids, and use the exact verifier only after the CA surrogate predicts complete forcing.
experiment_seed: Fix a small slope alphabet X with 4-6 nonzero vectors, enumerate tiny product grids, and compare surrogate infection closure against an exact global linear-algebra implementation.
novelty_claim: The new step is to encode arithmetic Kakeya forcing as a quotient-module infection process with a genuinely local state representation, making CA-style search plausible without discarding exactness.
differentiation: This is not another asymptotic Kakeya argument or another generic bootstrap-percolation paper. The target object is a concrete constructible certificate with score minimization, and the state variable is an integer module tied to the verifier semantics.

description: Treat edge labels as signed chip-transfer channels carrying slope mass between neighboring copies of a subgraph. A vertex is forced when local cancellations leave only anti-diagonal charge outside the already-infected region, so sandpile-style potentials can guide where sparse edges should concentrate or dissipate mass.
mathematical_formalization: A state is c: V -> Z^2 with legal moves c -> c + v(delta_u - delta_v) for each edge uv labelled v and c -> c + x delta_u for each initial seed x. Force e when c|_{V \ (T union {e})} = 0 and c(e) = a(1,-1), a != 0; search for edge layouts minimizing score while steering c toward such sparse anti-diagonal residues.
analogical_connections: Abelian sandpiles, except the conserved quantity is a 2-vector of slopes.
Electrical-network flow concentration with anti-diagonal current as the output signal.
Avalanche scheduling in self-organized critical systems.
implementation_hypothesis: Use a dual potential over vertices to estimate whether a proposed gluing pattern can focus enough anti-diagonal residue. Couple local search over edge labels to a fast chip-firing simulator and reject motifs whose potentials disperse too quickly.
experiment_seed: On fixed small constructible graphs, compare potential-guided edge mutations against uniform random mutations and track which search finds forceable instances faster.
novelty_claim: The new ingredient is a conserved-charge dual picture for arithmetic Kakeya certificates, intended to produce search heuristics and potentials rather than a direct theorem.
differentiation: Existing bootstrap-percolation papers optimize infection thresholds or times; this concept introduces vector-valued charge conservation and anti-diagonal concentration as the core search proxy.

description: Compile finite-time forcing into SAT or MaxSAT, viewing the initial singleton seeds and already-forced vertices as boundary controls for a cellular automaton. The solver searches jointly over edge labels, seeds, and infection schedules while minimizing m(G)+|R| under exact logical constraints.
mathematical_formalization: Introduce Boolean variables for edge labels, seed placements, time-layered infection events inf(e,t), and bounded coefficient choices for local derivations. Constrain inf(e,t+1) to hold iff inf(e,t) already holds or some allowed local certificate produces a(1,-1) at e using support inside T_t union {e}; minimize sum(edge_used) + sum(seed_used).
analogical_connections: Regional controllability, with R and T as actuators and forced vertices as the controlled region.
Bounded-horizon model checking for a discrete dynamical system.
Exact design of a circuit whose accepted trajectories are valid forcing proofs.
implementation_hypothesis: Start with a bounded horizon H and a tiny slope alphabet X, encode local derivations as pseudo-Boolean constraints, and add symmetry breaking on repeated copies in the constructible grammar. Use UNSAT cores to learn forbidden motifs and feed them back into the grammar search.
experiment_seed: Attempt exact synthesis on 2-layer and 3-layer product grids with small X, then benchmark whether MaxSAT can rediscover known near-bound motifs or prove small instances impossible.

closest_prior_art.title: Regional Controllability of Cellular Automata as a SAT Problem

novelty_claim: This would be the first exact SAT compilation of arithmetic Kakeya constructible certificates as steerable CA trajectories.
differentiation: It is not generic graph generation and not generic CA controllability: the Boolean model must encode integer-labelled edge differences, anti-diagonal detection, and the score objective from the verifier.

description: Use graph-grammar induction to search directly in the recursive language of constructible graphs instead of in flat adjacency lists. The goal is to mine reusable gluing productions that preserve forceability while compressing witness size and search branching factor.
mathematical_formalization: Let P be a production system whose rules have the form H -> glue(H_0,...,H_k; theta), where theta records identified vertices and inserted X-labelled edges. Optimize L(P) = score(P) + lambda |P| over grammars whose generated graphs admit full forcing, using positive examples from successful motifs and negative examples from stalled motifs.
analogical_connections: Developmental biology: the certificate grows by repeated local morphogenetic rules.
Macro-cell compilation: one validated local block becomes a reusable production.
Minimum-description-length modeling of constructive proofs.
implementation_hypothesis: Represent successful small graphs as derivation trees, cluster repeated glue patterns, and run beam search over candidate productions. Score grammars by how often they generate forceable substructures per unit complexity.
experiment_seed: Seed the search with hand-designed low-depth constructions, induce productions, and test whether induced grammars regenerate the seeds and extrapolate to larger forceable graphs.

closest_prior_art.title: Data-Efficient Graph Grammar Learning for Molecular Generation

novelty_claim: The novelty is to treat arithmetic Kakeya witnesses as a grammar-learning problem over proof-generating graph families, not as one-off graphs.
differentiation: Prior grammar work aims to imitate observed graph distributions. Here the grammar is judged by exact forceability and score, so it is a proof-search object rather than a generative-model benchmark.

description: Use e-graphs to discover reusable rewrite rules among slope expressions and local forcing lemmas. This compresses repeated linear manipulations across many candidate certificates and can suggest which low-complexity slopes are worth inserting into X.
mathematical_formalization: Build a DSL whose terms denote expressions obtained from singleton seeds, edge differences, and eliminations modulo forced support. Equality saturation maintains an e-graph of equivalent slope expressions, and a cost model C(term) rewards short derivations of a(1,-1) at target vertices.
analogical_connections: A proof assistant for local slope algebra.
Compiler superoptimization, except the target is anti-diagonal reachability.
Memoized Gaussian elimination over a shared proof forest.
implementation_hypothesis: Prototype a small rewrite DSL, infer candidate rules from successful exact derivations, and use saturation to canonicalize local proof obligations before they are passed into SAT or beam search.
experiment_seed: Collect exact derivations from tiny forceable instances, infer rewrite rules, and measure whether search branching shrinks on held-out instances with the learned rule set enabled.

closest_prior_art.title: Rewrite Rule Inference Using Equality Saturation
Sum-difference exponents for boundedly many slopes, and rational complexity

novelty_claim: The concept is new because it applies equality saturation to arithmetic Kakeya local proof algebra, turning hidden linear identities into searchable reusable lemmas.
differentiation: This is not a reimplementation of compiler-oriented e-graph work. The e-classes represent forcing obligations and slope identities, and the output is a smaller exact proof search space.

description: Use rational complexity as a curriculum variable for the slope set X and for when new labels are allowed to enter the local automaton. The search begins with low-complexity slopes that support many cheap local identities, and only expands X when the current CA dynamics provably stalls.
mathematical_formalization: Let kappa(x) be a rational-complexity penalty on nonzero x in X. Search over nested alphabets X_0 subset X_1 subset ... with objective score(G,R,T) + beta sum_{x in X} kappa(x); permit the transition X_j -> X_{j+1} only after the local closure operator on X_j reaches a fixed point without full forcing.
analogical_connections: Curriculum learning where the model earns new symbols only after exhausting the current alphabet.
Renormalization: start with coarse low-complexity slopes and refine only when necessary.
Morphogen stages in developmental systems.
implementation_hypothesis: Use Tao-style rational-complexity scoring to prioritize candidate slopes, couple that with the quotient-module CA, and prune any search branch that adds complexity before all simpler closure options are exhausted.
experiment_seed: Compare unrestricted slope mutation against the curriculum on identical beam-search budgets, and track score, number of unique local lemmas, and verifier success rate.

closest_prior_art.title: Sum-difference exponents for boundedly many slopes, and rational complexity
Intrinsically Motivated Discovery of Diverse Patterns in Self-Organizing Systems

novelty_claim: The new idea is to convert rational complexity from an analytic descriptor into a concrete control knob for certificate search and CA alphabet growth.
differentiation: The math papers study rational complexity analytically; the self-organization paper studies open-ended exploration. This concept merges them into an exact search prior for AK witnesses.

description: Derive a hypergraph whose hyperedges encode sufficient support patterns for anti-diagonal forcing, then deliberately search for long-running spanning processes. The hypothesis is that sparse but deep infection chains may recycle the same few edges many times and therefore beat denser, faster constructions on score.
mathematical_formalization: Let H_F have vertex set V(G) and hyperedges S -> e whenever there exists a local linear derivation that forces e from support contained in S union {e}. For a seed set A, let tau_H(A) be the number of rounds until closure; optimize score(G,R,T) while preferring larger tau_H(A) under the constraint cl_H(A) = V.
analogical_connections: A slow avalanche in bootstrap percolation rather than an immediate cascade.
Long proof chains that reuse a small axiom base many times.
Pipeline latency used as a proxy for structural reuse.
implementation_hypothesis: Extract approximate dependency hyperedges from the exact solver, estimate infection times quickly, and bias the outer search toward sparse constructions with unusually long closure time.
experiment_seed: On fixed small X, enumerate candidate graphs and compare score against derived hypergraph infection time to test whether longer-running instances systematically have better edge-to-coverage ratios.

closest_prior_art.title: On the Running Time of Hypergraph Bootstrap Percolation
The maximal running time of hypergraph bootstrap percolation

novelty_claim: The novelty is to treat infection time as a positive design feature for arithmetic Kakeya witnesses rather than as a complexity nuisance.
differentiation: The hypergraph papers study generic closure systems. Here the hyperedges come from exact integer-linear forcing semantics and are only a derived abstraction to guide witness search.

description: Train a graph cellular automaton to propose promising edge-label layouts, slope alphabets, and seed masks on constructible grids. The learned model is only a proposer; exact forceability is still checked by a symbolic verifier, but the proposal prior can drastically shrink the discrete search space.
mathematical_formalization: Let h_e^{t+1} = phi(h_e^t, Agg_{e_prime ~ e}(h_{e_prime}^t, ell_{e,e_prime})) be a graph-CA update on a candidate constructible graph. A decoder predicts edge labels, X-membership, and seed masks; train with loss L = surrogate_unforced + lambda score_proxy + mu verifier_disagreement.
analogical_connections: A learned developmental prior over proof certificates.
Graph neural architecture search, but for additive-combinatorial witnesses.
A stochastic proposal engine sitting in front of an exact theorem checker.
implementation_hypothesis: Generate exact small-instance data with SAT or exhaustive search, train the graph CA to imitate good certificates, and use it as a proposal distribution in a larger beam search over graphs and slope sets.
experiment_seed: Train on tiny 2-layer and 3-layer grids, then evaluate whether the learned proposer improves verifier hit rate on larger held-out grids relative to random or hand-crafted proposals.

closest_prior_art.title: HyperNCA: Growing Developmental Networks with Neural Cellular Automata

novelty_claim: No cited paper targets exact combinatorial proof certificates; the new piece is using graph NCA as a learned prior over AK witness space while keeping verification symbolic.
differentiation: This is not claiming that a neural CA proves the theorem by itself. The network only proposes candidate local structures that are then audited by the exact arithmetic-Kakeya verifier.

description: Use quality-diversity search instead of pure best-score optimization, preserving a library of distinct certificate motifs across slope complexity, infection time, symmetry type, and grammar depth. This is aimed at escaping the narrow basin around current near-best sum-difference constructions.
mathematical_formalization: Maintain an archive A[d] indexed by descriptors d(c) = (|X|, grammar_depth, infection_time, symmetry_rank, mean_rational_complexity). For each candidate c, fitness is f(c) = -score(c) plus a verifier bonus for exact forceability; store the highest-fitness candidate in each descriptor cell.
analogical_connections: MAP-Elites for proof motifs rather than robot morphologies.
An ecological niche model in which many different certificate species coexist.
Open-ended evolution over exact combinatorial structures.
implementation_hypothesis: Define mutation operators on X, d_i, partial f_i maps, and initial seeds, then run a QD archive with exact verifier feedback and a fast CA surrogate for triage. Use the archive to mine families that pure hill-climbing never visits.
experiment_seed: Compare QD against simulated annealing on identical compute budgets, tracking both best score and archive diversity in descriptors tied to arithmetic structure.

closest_prior_art.title: Toward Artificial Open-Ended Evolution within Lenia using Quality-Diversity
Intrinsically Motivated Discovery of Diverse Patterns in Self-Organizing Systems
CAX: Cellular Automata Accelerated in JAX

novelty_claim: The innovation is to treat exact arithmetic certificates as an open-ended dynamical search domain with mathematically meaningful descriptors, rather than optimizing a single objective from the start.
differentiation: The cited work targets visually or dynamically interesting CA patterns. Here the archive dimensions are proof-structural quantities, and every elite is judged by an exact symbolic checker.

description: Use negative results about affine cellular automata to prune search families that are too linear to isolate anti-diagonal residue effectively. The idea is to reserve nonlinearity for thresholded forcing decisions or grammar-level branching, rather than wasting time on affine surrogates that are structurally incapable of rich behavior.
mathematical_formalization: If a surrogate update rule U on local states is affine over F_p, then the reachable configuration family remains in an affine closure C_U. Reject any surrogate family whose invariants imply that isolated anti-diagonal detection cannot break out of C_U; require a nonlinear gate g(M_e) = 1[(1,-1) intersects M_e nontrivially] or grammar-level branching to enter the search space.
analogical_connections: Using an impossibility theorem as an architecture prior.
Circuit lower bounds guiding which model class is worth training.
A theorem-driven regularizer for local dynamical systems.
implementation_hypothesis: Characterize the algebraic form of each local surrogate rule, reject affine and near-affine variants before expensive search, and log which nonlinear components are actually responsible for improvements in verifier success.
experiment_seed: Ablate search with and without the affine-family filter, and measure whether rejected families indeed fail to produce complete forcing on small exact instances.

closest_prior_art.title: Simulation Limitations of Affine Cellular Automata
Regional Controllability of Cellular Automata as a SAT Problem

novelty_claim: The new contribution is methodological: use automata-theoretic impossibility results to shape the certificate-search model class before optimization begins.
differentiation: This is not a theorem claiming AK witnesses cannot arise from affine dynamics. It is a practical search prior that treats affine limitations as a reason to bias architecture and grammar design.
